title: Minimum Difference Between Largest and Smallest Value in Three Moves
summary: Given an integer array nums, you can change at most one element to any value in a single move.
statement: Given an integer array nums, you can change at most one element to any value in a single move. Perform up to three such moves to minimize the difference between the largest and smallest values in the array. Return the smallest possible difference.
constraints: In one move, replace any one value with any other value; make at most three moves.
Minimize the difference between the final maximum and minimum.
hints: Only values at the sorted extremes ever need replacement.
Distribute three changes between the low and high ends in four possible ways.
Compute the remaining range for 3/0, 2/1, 1/2, and 0/3 removals.
Replacing removed extremes inside the surviving range realizes each case; changing an interior value cannot improve either boundary.
editorial: Replacing removed extremes inside the surviving range realizes each case; changing an interior value cannot improve either boundary.

tests.explanation: All but one value can be changed to match, so four or fewer values always yield zero.
Changing one, zero, and fourteen leaves values five and ten, whose range is five.
